items.stem: How many bytes are there in one kibibyte (KiB)?
items.markingKey: 1 KiB = 2¹⁰ bytes = 1024 bytes; 1 kB = 1000 bytes.

items.stem: Explain why a storage device advertised as 500 GB appears smaller when its capacity is shown by an operating system in GiB.
items.answer: The manufacturer uses decimal prefixes (1 GB = 10⁹ bytes) but the operating system reports binary prefixes (1 GiB = 2³⁰ bytes). Since 2³⁰ > 10⁹, the same number of bytes gives a smaller number of GiB (about 466 GiB).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: GB = 10⁹ bytes; 1 mark: GiB = 2³⁰ bytes, which is larger; 1 mark: so the same capacity is a smaller number of GiB [3]

items.stem: Explain why hexadecimal is often used by programmers instead of binary.
items.answer: Hexadecimal is shorter and easier to read, write and remember; there are fewer errors when copying; each hex digit maps directly onto 4 bits so conversion is simple.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 2: shorter/easier to read; fewer errors; direct 4-bit mapping [2]

items.stem: Use run-length encoding to compress the string RRRRRRGGBBRRRR. Give each run as a count followed by the character.
items.answer: 6R 2G 2B 4R
items.markingKey: Runs: 6R 2G 2B 4R [2]

items.stem: Samuel records a mono sound clip lasting 5 seconds at a sampling rate of 32 kHz and a sampling resolution of 16 bits. Calculate the file size in MB (1 MB = 1 000 000 bytes).
